table_8_1_notes: For inputs between listed figures use the next largest listed input. Round-duct sizes assume a maximum equivalent duct length of 20 ft; for over 20 ft up to 50 ft, increase the round duct by one size. A rectangular duct may not have a dimension under 3 in, so rectangular free area is never under 9 in2 (Clause 8.3.2).

clause_8_4.with_draft_control: 1 in2 per 7,000 Btu/h up to and including 1,000,000 Btu/h, plus 1 in2 per 14,000 Btu/h in excess (8.4.2); opening at or ducted to 6-18 in above floor level.
clause_8_4.power_burner_no_draft_control: 1 in2 per 30,000 Btu/h of total rated input (8.4.3).
clause_8_4.ventilation_opening: At the highest practicable point: at least 10% of the supply-opening area and never less than 10 in2 (8.4.1), in addition to the supply opening.

enclosure_openings_8_2_6: Appliance enclosure inside a loose-construction structure: opening(s) with free area at least 1 in2 per 1,000 Btu/h of total input, 6-18 in above floor; plus, where any appliance has a draft-control device, a second opening of the same free area as near the ceiling as practicable.
not_covered: Table 8.2 grid (no draft control, tight construction, up to 400 MBH) and the volume-based Tables 8.3/8.4 (loose construction) are not reproduced — their full grids could not be verified from public sources. Two verified Table 8.2 points: 125 MBH -> 9 in2; 200 MBH -> 14 in2.
louvre_rules: Free area is gross area minus louvre/grille/screen blockage (8.5.1); louvre apertures no dimension under 1/4 in (8.5.2); no manually operated dampers or adjustable louvres (8.5.3); automatic dampers must be interlocked with the burner (8.5.4).
source: CSA B149.1 Clause 8 (B149.1-05 text and BC Campus gas-fitter textbook), verified 2026-11-15
